newsitem.title: JAPAN: E.Asia Grains-Japan to step up U.S. corn purchases.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grains-Japan to step up U.S. corn purchases.

text.p: Japanese corn importers are seen stepping up their buying of U.S. corn this week ahead of the mid-August holiday season, dealers said on Monday.
"We'll gradually step up buying for the fourth quarter period this week," a Japanese trader said.
The Japanese have covered up to 30 percent of their U.S. corn needs for the last quarter of 1997, he added.
Corn premiums were being quoted in Japan at nearly 98 U.S. cents a bushel over CBOT September futures.

In South Korea, flour milling companies are said to have recently bought between 40,000-50,000 tonnes of Australian wheat during July for September shipment in negotiations with the Australian Wheat Board (AWB).
"It is very difficult to know how much Australian wheat has been sold to domestic flour millers since the buyers are directly negotiating with the AWB," a trader with a flour milling company said.
The trader said South Korean buyers are buying about 600,000 tonnes of Australian wheat, which would account for around 30 percent of the country's total purchase of around 2.0 million tonnes a year.
Two Korean flour millers are expected to buy a 20,000-tonne cargo of U.S. wheat for shipment between September to October if futures prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) ease.
Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd passed on a joint tender last week to buy 22,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat due to higher-than-expected prices.
But Korean buyers will probably put their grain purchases on hold during the seasonally slow summer period as buyers leave for their annual holidays this week, traders said.
"Our clients are saying there will be a quiet market for grains from the end of July till early August due to summer holidays," a trader said.
Traders said most Korean corn buyers would stay on the sidelines for the time being as they have adequate coverage out to October.

An official with Korea's Pan Ocean Shipping Co Ltd said freight rates for Panamax-sized cargoes for August shipment from the U.S. Pacific Northwest fell to US$12.50 a tonne due to slow demand from last week's $13.50-$14.00 a tonne.
Rates from the U.S. Gulf for August shipment of Panamax-sized vessels fell to $22 a tonne from the previous week's rate of $23.50-$24.00 a tonne.
